<reason>Side B kept a live rebuttable-priority rule: residents' relational interests are part of the public interest, so economic edge needs to show substantial harm to justify separation. Side A never answered that selective-accounting point and conceded a modest edge does not justify parent-child separation, then failed to justify limiting the motion to queuing for spouses/partners beyond assertion. A's inheritance/chain and stewardship points were strong but blunted by B's dependency limits and severity test.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's pressure that a modest fiscal edge must justify years of separation forced A's A1 concession of a humanitarian floor, which B then used to show economic return is not decisive and that A's urgent-needs exception is a normal rebuttable priority, not a surrender.</best_rebuttal>
